summary: Verified that effective max_running_requests can exceed the independently derived decode CUDA graph ceiling and added a one-time startup warning without changing scheduling policy. The exact L40/Qwen latency transition was not reproducible on the assigned AMD gfx950 hardware.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: the issue values resolved to 4096 requests versus graph max batch 32, but the unmodified implementation emitted no warning (1 failed, 2 passed).
Passing-after regression and adjacent memory-pool coverage: 44 tests and 7 subtests passed, including issue arithmetic, equal-capacity, disabled-graph, and warn-once behavior.
All configured formatting, lint, syntax, registry, and repository policy hooks passed for the changed source and test.
Real gfx950 engine startup and decode graph capture for batches 1 and 2; startup warned for effective request capacity 4; four HTTP probes returned 200 and the owned process group was reaped.
On AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2/HIP 7.2.26015, the GPU dot product was 32.0 and exactly matched the independent CPU reference 32.0.

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-ee32a0b3d017/raw/gpu-graph-final/server.log records gfx950 decode graph capture and the new capacity warning; probe-summary.json records four HTTP 200 responses; gpu-numerical-reference.json records device identity and an exact numerical reference match.
remaining_limitations: The reported NVIDIA L40 and Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct weights/ShareGPT workload were unavailable, so the 4x latency transition and absorbing-state dynamics were not reproduced.
The deterministic tiny random Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only; it does not qualify Qwen architecture behavior, semantic accuracy, or a distributed workload.

The correction is diagnostic: it exposes the unsafe default relationship at startup but does not choose between reducing admission and increasing graph capture, whose latency and memory tradeoffs are workload-dependent.
No native library was changed or rebuilt.
